intended_object: The inclusion functor Δ₊ ↪ Δ, from the semi-simplex category (finite ordinals [n] with injective order-preserving maps) to the simplex category (the same objects with all order-preserving maps). Inferred from the docstring and the module.
explanation: On objects the functor sends ⦋n⦌ₛ to ⦋n⦌. On morphisms it sends an order embedding Fin (n+1) ↪o Fin (m+1) to its underlying monotone map, which is a morphism in SimplexCategory. The functor laws hold by definition and are discharged automatically: identities go to identities and composition (`trans`) goes to composition. This is exactly the standard inclusion of the wide subcategory of injective maps into Δ. The rest of the file confirms it: the functor is faithful, its image is the monomorphisms, and `homOfMono` gives the inverse on monomorphisms. The construction concerns these specific categories, so the question of generality does not arise.
